implementerProof.how: Every proof the implement handoff carries was driven again from my own builds on this pod, none of it read from its files: acceptance A5 over the HTTP API on ten LINUX specs with a control run on EACH side rather than only on the base; three alternating base-then-head replay pairs of my own; the three profile shares re-read from my own six profiles; the heaps from my own pairs; go test -race on the docs package here; and both of its negative controls reproduced by making the break myself. Each came out as it reported. Two places where my reading is stricter than its own and the handoff should be read with mine: its A1 says rule (i) does not hold at its pair because one head run sat above one base run, where all six of mine separate cleanly, so the strict rule holds on my pairs and spec v25's holds on both; and its A4 benchmark line carries the preallocation alone, which is right, because that benchmark validates on both sides - the validation a reused finder skips is measured in my A4's second benchmark and nowhere else.

The whole-tree fingerprint moves on AGENTS.md prose and on the merges' own text and is the wrong instrument for that question.

proof.criterion: A4 (benchmark half), the quote finder: B/op and ns/op down with identical ranges. The branch makes two separate changes to the finder and one measurement cannot carry both, so this is two benchmarks.
proof.surface: the pmdoc package on a 657 KB LINUX spec of the replay bundle, in worktrees at base 5330bcb2 and head 6db39f4d
proof.command: LOADTEST_BENCH_SPEC=<657 KB spec> LOADTEST_BENCH_QUOTES=<seven sentences> GOMAXPROCS=2 GOWORK=off go test ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkA4 -benchtime 40x -count 5
proof.observed: The preallocation, one-shot FindQuote (which rebuilds the flattened text every call and validates on BOTH sides, so it carries C4 alone): ns/op base 93.3 / 85.9 / 100.2 / 102.8 / 99.3 ms against head 61.1 / 53.4 / 73.4 / 72.8 / 35.5 ms; B/op 37,392,375-37,394,231 against 10,769,657-10,777,076, -71%; allocs/op 14,314 against 14,216; the range found identical in all ten runs, 612585..612645. The validation skip, measured WITHIN the head build because ValidDocument.QuoteFinder exists on no other - one finder resolving seven quotes of the one document, NewQuoteFinder against ValidDocument.QuoteFinder: 44.9 / 43.0 / 48.5 / 46.5 / 45.4 ms against 40.3 / 38.5 / 45.1 / 42.9 / 43.1 ms, medians 45.4 against 42.9, with B/op identical at 10.77 MB. So the skip is real but small, about 5% of a reused finder and no allocation at all, and the preallocation is what moves the number. The branch carries no committed FindQuote benchmark; both of these are throwaways of mine, deleted after the run.
proof.negativeControl: The two benchmarks are each other's control for the claim they are kept apart to stop: the one-shot comparison cannot see the validation skip, since it validates on both sides, and the reused comparison cannot see the preallocation, since both of its arms are the same build. A single benchmark reported as 'all of C4' would have been true of neither half. The ranges, identical on both builds and in every run, are the control on the finder answering the same thing while it answers it faster.

observations: Read CI, never re-ran it: run 41185900963 at code head 6db39f4d, whole-run success. Three re-pin drains replaced this pod during this issue's testing and each destroyed a measurement held only on its disk - the second cost four of six completed A1 runs. This round was run as one unattended script with a checkpoint after every stage, and each A1 step directory was uploaded to the issue as its run ended. The first checkpoint still failed: the A5 archive was 184 MB because it carried four normalised record files of 158 MB each, and the artifact limit is 25 MB. I repacked the report, the quotes and the harness (8 KB) and uploaded that. A checkpoint is not a checkpoint until it has run once.

The measurement spans two heads by the architect's ruling of 09:29Z: the pairs and A5 were taken at 1c9ce28b and the head is now 6db39f4d, which merges main for #2598 and changes no Go. I verified that rather than accepting it - the Go half of the branch's own diff against main is 1b8fd788ae228f9e2a0aa5f793ea63b12c7e827a0d91cff1bfb3f0a493361753 at e4118455, 1c9ce28b, 6db39f4d and c7c9fec0 alike. All three A1 pairs compare the same two builds, base 5330bcb2 against head 1c9ce28b, each pair run base then head back to back on one pod, as the architect's pair rule requires.

For whoever writes the next plan on this harness: legion/INFRA-639 no longer exists on origin (#2466 merged), so every command in this issue's plan naming `packages/envoy/loadtest on legion/INFRA-639 at 4f53011a` names a branch that is gone. The harness is main's, and replay-get needs LOADTEST_REPLAY_ISSUE=INFRA-639 to find the bundle's parts.

One unexplained event, recorded rather than diagnosed: a replay-prepare died with `Dispatch exited while the block index still owed 1320 entries` and a clean `shutting down` line in its log - a SIGTERM, not a crash, with 16 GB free. Each role's own PID namespace hides whatever sent it, the same blindness as the port bug INFRA-639 owns. A straight retry ran past that point and completed. If a prepare dies that way again, retry it once before looking for a cause.
